claims.hypothesis: The nuclear-scale concentration of cold molecular gas depends on AGN X-ray luminosity, with a turnover indicating AGN feedback
claims.experiment: CCI = log10(Sigma50/Sigma200) from CO images of 45 AGN and 19 non-AGN, binned in L_X and fitted with MARS
claims.result: Turnover at log L_X = 41.51+/-0.31; feedback-branch slope -0.36+/-0.08 (about 4.5 sigma); build-up slope consistent with flat
claims.finding: Two branches (AGN build-up and AGN feedback) in the CCI-L_X plane, confirming the earlier GATOS result on a larger sample

evidence.quote: shows a statistically significant turnover at a luminosity breakpoint $L_{\rm X}\simeq10^{41.5}$erg s$^{-1}$, which divides the sample into two branches

claims.hypothesis: The radial shape of the cold gas profile changes with L_X
claims.experiment: Median normalised CO radial profiles per L_X bin with KS tests between bins
claims.result: Flat or inverted profiles at high L_X, highly concentrated profiles in the build-up peak; KS p<=0.001
claims.finding: Profile shapes track the CCI trend

evidence.quote: The profiles appear as flat or inverted in the AGN feedback branch galaxies.

claims.hypothesis: The turnover is robust to the choice of statistic
claims.experiment: Gini coefficient of the CO radial profiles over 0-200 pc
claims.result: G correlates with CCI (Spearman ~0.85) and anticorrelates with mean radius (~-0.94), with a similar turnover
claims.finding: The non-parametric analysis confirms the CCI result

evidence.quote: The radial Gini coefficients are shown to be strongly correlated with the molecular gas concentration.

claims.hypothesis: Hot H2 shows the same concentration turnover as cold gas
claims.experiment: HCI from SINFONI/OSIRIS H2 2.12 um maps for 35 targets, MARS fit
claims.result: Turnover at log L_X = 42.04+/-0.27; feedback-branch slope -0.29+/-0.11 (about 2.6 sigma); range 0.46 dex versus 0.63 dex for CCI
claims.finding: Hot gas shows a qualitatively similar but weaker trend, so the decrease mainly affects the cold phase

evidence.quote: shows a qualitatively similar but less pronounced turnover compared to the trend shown by the $CCI$ index

claims.hypothesis: Hot gas compensates the nuclear-scale cold gas deficit in the highest-L_X AGN
claims.experiment: Hot-to-cold mass surface density ratio at r<=50 pc and r<=200 pc for 42 map pairs
claims.result: ~1.5-2 increase of the ratio on nuclear scales beyond the turnover, with hot/cold mass fraction <=1e-4
claims.finding: The hot gas does not account for the missing cold gas

evidence.quote: However, this twofold increase does not compensate for the nuclear-scale deficit of cold molecular gas mass identified in the highest luminosity AGN.

claims.hypothesis: The two branches are connected by an evolutionary cycle of gas build-up, feedback and starvation
claims.experiment: Analytic transit and exhaustion timescale estimates for four feedback-branch galaxies, bar fractions and N_H-Eddington ratio location
claims.result: t_transit and t_exhaustion ~1 to a few 10 Myr
claims.finding: A tentative scenario with short transit, exhaustion and starvation timescales

evidence.quote: We present a tentative scenario describing an evolutionary link connecting the galaxies analyzed in this work.

evidence.quote: While the values of $R_{\rm 31}$, $R_{\rm 21}$ for the galaxies in our sample are not constrained
Under these extreme hypotheses the total uncertainty would amount to $\pm$0.20 dex.

limitations_admitted.value: The increase of CCI along the AGN build-up branch is not statistically significant

evidence.quote: However, we note that given the associated error bars, the reported increase in $CCI$ among the galaxies of the AGN build-up branch is not statistically significant.
Within the limits of our admittedly small statistics

referee_caveats_inferred: CO images have heterogeneous resolution, sensitivity and recoverable scale (median 36 pc beam versus a 50 pc nuclear aperture), so CCI may be resolution-dependent; no common-resolution test is described
A single set of R31, R21 and alpha_CO from NGC 1068 and the Milky Way is applied to all galaxies, so any real nuclear excitation or conversion-factor gradient with L_X would bias the trend
L_X (2-10 keV) is a snapshot proxy for a variable AGN; Eddington ratios are only available for 27 galaxies
Bins hold only 8-9 data sets, some galaxies appear several times (e.g. NGC 7172, NGC 5728), so points are not fully independent
The evolutionary scenario is inferred from a cross-section of different galaxies, not tracked in time
Selection from several heterogeneous surveys may introduce bias; early-type galaxies from WISDOM are excluded by choice

missing_for_reproduction: Per-image CO data products and their reduction recipes (deferred to about a dozen earlier papers)
Per-galaxy L_X bin assignments and the exact MARS settings
Per-galaxy NIR H2 line fluxes and apertures
Outflow rates and torus masses used in the timescale estimates (taken from other papers)
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Raw data for ~25 ALMA projects would be hundreds of GB to TB; starting from released survey CO cubes or moment maps (e.g. PHANGS-ALMA, GATOS) would be tens of GB
reproducibility.score_reason: Final concentration indices per galaxy and many numeric results are tabulated, but the CO images come from many earlier papers whose reduction is not described, and the MARS and bootstrap settings are not given; no code or data release is stated.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The CO imaging and per-galaxy extraction are inherited from other papers and not specified here, so the recipe is too incomplete to redo from the paper alone, even though the final tables are numeric.

methods_papers.why: Defined the nuclear/CND concentration index and first found the two-branch trend in the GATOS sample; this paper follows its methodology
LINEFIT code used to extract the H2 2.12 um line flux from SINFONI cubes

companion_papers.why: Applied the GB21 concentration index to the WISDOM sample, including many early-type galaxies
NGC 7172 case study providing CO data and torus mass used here
